EUCA S
NO LAUGHING MATTER
It was no laughing matter, at least to Carl
Marchese (right) Chief Steward for Wiscon-
sin Auto Racing, Inc. as he talked to Ray
Nichels, Highland, Ind., manager of the trio
of 1962 Pontiacs driven by Paul Goldsmith,
A. J. Foyt, and Roger Ward in the 200 mile
stock car race that day. Nichels had reason
to smile. Foyt had nailed down third place,
Goldsmith, fifth place, in the July 15 Classic
that paid more than $25,000 in prize and ac-
cessory money.
BOB MEANS PHOTO
44 YEARS OF RACING KNOW-HOW
Nearly a half-century of
racing know-how was concen-
trated in the conversation be-
tween Henry Banks, Director
of Competition for the United
States Auto Club and Norm
Nelson, Racine, second rank-
ing USAC late model stock
car driver just before the July
15 200 mile stock car race here.
Banks raced 21 years in big
cars and midgets. Was national
AAA big car champion in
1950. Nelson, in his 23rd year
since he drove his first race is
the acknowledged king of the
stocks at Milwaukee with
seven victories and more than
$45,000 in gross earnings to
his credit. He was National
USAC Stock Car Champ in
1960.
DICK JOHNSON PHOTO

Two Chicago area drivers who have been frequent competitors in late model stock car races here are
Ken Finley, Bridgeview and Rich Sutkus, Oak Lawn. Both qualified for starting positions in the July 15 200
mile stock car grind here. Finley, driving a 1962 Pontiac set up by Ray Nichels Engineering Co. finished 12th.
Sutkus discovered a broken valve in his engine just after his time trial and was unable to start the event in
his 1960 Ford.
